web_evidence.title: 28 Summers by Elin Hilderbrand | Excerpt | Bookreporter.com
web_evidence.note: A sustained excerpt covers the prologue and the start of Part One through external narration of Link and Mallory, including access to their thoughts. The occasional inclusive authorial 'we' does not participate as a story character.

web_evidence.title: Living in an Elin Hilderbrand Novel
web_evidence.note: Kirkus discusses the novel's chapters from several characters' points of view and its direct-addressing authorial voice; Hilderbrand identifies the technique as an omniscient narrator. This establishes nonparticipating third-person base narration across the novel.

web_evidence.title: Quote by John Green: “It is May of 2020...”
web_evidence.note: The exact text of q04581 is attributed to John Green's The Anthropocene Reviewed, demonstrating cross-title contamination in quotes.csv.

web_evidence.title: The Anthropocene Reviewed Book — John Green
web_evidence.note: John Green's official site identifies The Anthropocene Reviewed as a memoiristic essay collection rating subjects on a five-star scale, matching the quote set's recurring personal reviews rather than the characters and plot of 28 Summers.

web_evidence.title: Dutton Launches John Green’s First Nonfiction Book, THE ANTHROPOCENE REVIEWED
web_evidence.note: The publisher confirms that Green's book consists of personal essays reflecting on humanity, corroborating the provenance mismatch indicated by the quote corpus.

search_log: Searched “28 Summers Elin Hilderbrand excerpt first chapter” and opened the sustained Bookreporter excerpt.
Searched “28 Summers point of view narrator third person” and “28 Summers omniscient narrator”; opened the Kirkus interview with Hilderbrand, which resolved the multiple-POV omniscient structure.
Searched the exact phrase “It is May of 2020, and I do not have a brain well suited for this”; the result attributes it to John Green's The Anthropocene Reviewed rather than 28 Summers.

Searched official John Green and Penguin Random House pages for The Anthropocene Reviewed; their descriptions of memoiristic five-star essays, including subjects such as sunsets and Canada geese, match the supplied quote corpus.
Checked Hachette's 28 Summers title pages; they verified the target title, author, characters, and plot but supplied synopsis rather than diagnostic prose.

Searched for interior excerpts and previews; page-flip copies and other unauthorized or synopsis-only results were discarded. The official Penguin sample for the contaminating title was too large for the web reader.
person_note: The supplied quotes are cross-title contamination from John Green's The Anthropocene Reviewed and therefore provide no valid person evidence for 28 Summers. Independent web evidence nevertheless establishes 28 Summers as third-person omniscient narration moving among several character viewpoints. Its authorial narrator sometimes says 'we' and addresses the reader, but that voice does not participate in Mallory and Jake's story, so it remains THIRD rather than FIRST or ALTERNATING. The only material limitation is the absence of target-aligned Goodreads quotes; the sustained excerpt and author interview independently agree.
